question: Which statement best describes Main property?
options: `float: left` moves an element to the left side of its containing area. Text and inline content can flow around it. It is like placing a photo beside a magazine paragraph. Use it for this text-wrapping effect, not as a general alignment system. For example, a floated image in an article can have text wrap beside it.

Content can wrap beside a floated item until it reaches the item’s height or a clearing boundary. This can make later sections unexpectedly move alongside the float. It is like text wrapping around an image on a printed page. Inspect the whole surrounding layout when adding floats. For example, a following heading may need clear when it must begin beneath that image.

`clear` tells an element to move below floats on one or both sides. It is like starting a new paragraph after the picture ends. Older layouts often used clearing techniques to contain floats; modern layout systems usually provide simpler ways to arrange components. For example, if the parent collapses around floats, use a modern containment approach or layout system.

Floated children may not contribute to a parent’s height in the way beginners expect. This can make the parent appear empty and allow later content to overlap. It is like stacking a picture outside the box used to measure the page. Understand the containing layout before mixing floats with other rules. For example, do not use floats to align a navigation bar or card grid.
